name: Hospital Scheduling System — Product & Engineering Sync

items.text: First version is for outpatient appointments at Greenfield Hospital
Receptionists creating appointments come first; most older patients call the hospital
Basic accessibility checks are part of the first release; patient interface accessible with large text and straightforward navigation
Slots consider room availability: a slot is unavailable if the doctor or the room is unavailable; no two consultations in the same room at the same time
Configurable buffer duration per department, not extra time after every appointment
Date-based list of appointments for patients and staff; calendar revisited later
Keep the component architecture flexible enough to add a calendar later
Patients can cancel their appointments
Cancellation window configurable per department with a default of two hours
Receptionists can override the cancellation cutoff; manual overrides record the staff member and the reason
Patients receive a cancellation notification by SMS
Abstract the SMS provider; do not couple the appointment service to a particular SMS vendor
SMS only for the first release: no email notifications, WhatsApp parked
Send a reminder twenty-four hours before an appointment
For appointments created less than twenty-four hours ahead, send the confirmation immediately and skip the reminder if its time has passed
Idempotency key on appointment ID and notification type prevents duplicate reminders on retries
When an appointment time changes, invalidate the queued reminder and schedule a new one
On a doctor's emergency leave, do not move appointments to another doctor automatically; list affected appointments for receptionists to contact patients
New 'rescheduling required' status: affected appointments keep their doctor, are not treated as confirmed and are not cancelled automatically
Do not automatically offer a freed slot to the next patient on the waitlist
Core scheduling model supports rooms, department buffers, cancellation rules and rescheduling status
Waitlist automation is not required for the initial release
Care plans are outside the scope of this release
Staff booking overlapping appointments get a warning and must confirm (override)
Patient self-service booking blocks overlapping appointments unless an explicitly supported exception
Log overlap overrides with staff member, timestamp and reason
Audit trail for appointment creation, cancellation, rescheduling and manual overrides
Audit records are append-only; ordinary users cannot edit or delete them through the API
Doctors see only their own schedules, not other patients' information
Receptionists manage appointments across their authorized departments; administrators configure departments, rooms, doctors and scheduling policies
Department-level access control enforced by the backend, not just hidden buttons
No medical history or clinical notes; store only enough to identify and contact the patient
Patient name, contact number and an identifier from the hospital's existing system
Pilot supports manual patient registration, with the integration point kept separate
Phone-number verification for patient self-service instead of accounts and passwords, subject to security review approval
Self-service built behind a feature flag and not enabled until the security review approves it
Internal demonstration by the end of October, then staff testing, then decide on a patient pilot
Basic summary with appointment and cancellation counts; no charts, exports or department comparisons in the first release
Summary includes a count of appointments requiring rescheduling
Waiting-time analytics parked for a later phase
No offline editing in the first release
Print-friendly view of the daily schedule for receptionists
Change slot-generation logic to account for room availability
Update the appointment state model with the rescheduling-required status
Test a doctor becoming unavailable after appointments are booked
Understand how receptionists currently manage waitlists
Keep the schema from blocking waitlists being added later
Make the overlap warning explicit with the conflicting appointment details so receptionists know they are overriding
Make audit records append-only at the application level
Test direct API access for permissions and that audit records cannot be edited or deleted
Arrange anonymized sample schedules and examples of common scheduling conflicts from different departments
Keep the initial reporting endpoints simple
Add a print-layout check to the acceptance tests
Document the API contracts once the appointment states are finalized
Build the daily schedule, appointment creation and cancellation screens
Review the patient flow for accessibility and make the status labels understandable
Coordinate with receptionists to validate the proposed workflows
Test plan covering appointment conflicts, permissions, audit records and notification retries
Which SMS provider to use; not selected yet
Waitlist automation undecided: how long to hold a slot and what if the notification arrives late
Patient self-service depends on the security review approving phone-number verification
Integration with the hospital's existing patient management system is not finalized
Whether it is ready for a patient pilot, decided after staff testing
Which overlapping appointments (consultation then diagnostic test) are valid exceptions
Appointments run longer than scheduled, e.g. fifteen-minute cardiology consultations taking thirty
Blocking extra time after every appointment would destroy capacity
Last-minute cancellations without visibility for staff
Waitlist slot holds introduce reservation locks and race conditions; two patients could claim the same slot
Notification worker retries could send duplicate reminders
If the internet goes down at reception, staff still need to see the day's appointments
Ordinary users could edit or delete audit records through the API
Disputes about who changed an appointment
End-of-October demonstration achievable only if the scope stays tight
Older patients phone the hospital and will not use an app
